findings.description: The FR-2 entry states the verdict-derive contract as: the trailer is INCONSISTENT when `rejected_summary` is non-empty and "a non-array summary or an unparseable envelope is a violation". The same entry, and the implementation report ("legacy envelopes (no `rejected_summary`, or `null`) pinned as passing"; "a pre-FR-2 envelope ... counts no sidecar rows as old as itself"), say a `null` or absent `rejected_summary` is the legacy pass. `null` is a non-array value, so the published contract sentence contradicts the legacy rule the code implements.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or a downstream check that reads the CHANGELOG as the `verdict-derive.sh` contract expects an envelope with `rejected_summary: null` to fail the trailer check, while the script passes it as a pre-FR-2 envelope. Historical-sprint triage decisions and any tooling built on the stated rule diverge from the code's actual verdict.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the sentence: "a present, non-null `rejected_summary` that is not an array, or an unparseable envelope, is a violation; a `null` or absent summary is read as a pre-FR-2 envelope (legacy pass)".

findings.description: The known-failures entry documents a refusal class that did not exist before: `kf-write-lib.sh new` now exits 1 with nothing written for titles that were previously accepted (non-UTF-8, `_emphasis_`, links, HTML tags, character references, backtick runs, padded code spans, a closing `#`, anchor-ambiguous codepoints, and any non-ASCII title when python3 is missing or fails). The entry itself labels this a "Behaviour change" yet is filed under `### Fixed` with no upgrade note, unlike the FR-2 entry directly above it which carries one.
findings.failure_mode: Automation or operators that invoke `kf-write-lib.sh new` with titles in any of the newly refused classes get exit 1 and no ledger entry; a caller that only scans `### Changed` for behaviour changes before upgrading does not learn of the new refusal, and the entry gives no remedy (how to rewrite a refused title, or that python3 is now required for non-ASCII titles).
findings.suggested_fix: Move the behaviour-change sentence under `### Changed` (or add an Upgrade note to the entry) stating that python3 is required for non-ASCII titles and that a refused title must be rewritten in plain text before the entry is written; keep the anchor-slug repair itself under `### Fixed`.
